NKJV.1: Abraham again took a wife, and her name was Keturah.
NKJV.2: And she bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
NKJV.3: Jokshan begot Sheba and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
NKJV.4: And the sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abidah, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah.
NKJV.5: And Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac.
NKJV.6: But Abraham gave gifts to the sons of the concubines which Abraham had; and while he was still living he sent them eastward, away from Isaac his son, to the country of the east.
NKJV.7: This is the sum of the years of Abraham’s life which he lived: one hundred and seventy-five years.
NKJV.8: Then Abraham breathed his last and died in a good old age, an old man and full of years, and was gathered to his people.
NKJV.9: And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, which is before Mamre, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite,
NKJV.10: the field which Abraham purchased from the sons of Heth. There Abraham was buried, and Sarah his wife.
NKJV.11: And it came to pass, after the death of Abraham, that God blessed his son Isaac. And Isaac dwelt at Beer Lahai Roi.
NKJV.12: Now this is the genealogy of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s maidservant, bore to Abraham.
NKJV.13: And these were the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations: The firstborn of Ishmael, Nebajoth; then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
NKJV.15: Hadar, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
NKJV.16: These were the sons of Ishmael and these were their names, by their towns and their settlements, twelve princes according to their nations.
NKJV.17: These were the years of the life of Ishmael: one hundred and thirty-seven years; and he breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people.
NKJV.18: (They dwelt from Havilah as far as Shur, which is east of Egypt as you go toward Assyria.) He died in the presence of all his brethren.
NKJV.19: This is the genealogy of Isaac, Abraham’s son. Abraham begot Isaac.
NKJV.20: Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah as wife, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Padan Aram, the sister of Laban the Syrian.
NKJV.21: Now Isaac pleaded with the LORD for his wife, because she was barren; and the LORD granted his plea, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
NKJV.22: But the children struggled together within her; and she said, “If all is well, why am I like this?” So she went to inquire of the LORD.
NKJV.23: And the LORD said to her: “Two nations are in your womb, Two peoples shall be separated from your body; One people shall be stronger than the other, And the older shall serve the younger.”
NKJV.24: So when her days were fulfilled for her to give birth, indeed there were twins in her womb.
NKJV.25: And the first came out red. He was like a hairy garment all over; so they called his name Esau.
NKJV.26: Afterward his brother came out, and his hand took hold of Esau’s heel; so his name was called Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them.
NKJV.27: So the boys grew. And Esau was a skillful hunter, a man of the field; but Jacob was a mild man, dwelling in tents.
NKJV.28: And Isaac loved Esau because he ate of his game, but Rebekah loved Jacob.
NKJV.29: Now Jacob cooked a stew; and Esau came in from the field, and he was weary.
NKJV.30: And Esau said to Jacob, “Please feed me with that same red stew, for I am weary.” Therefore his name was called Edom.
NKJV.31: But Jacob said, “Sell me your birthright as of this day.”
NKJV.32: And Esau said, “Look, I am about to die; so what is this birthright to me?”
NKJV.33: Then Jacob said, “Swear to me as of this day.” So he swore to him, and sold his birthright to Jacob.
NKJV.34: And Jacob gave Esau bread and stew of lentils; then he ate and drank, arose, and went his way. Thus Esau despised his birthright.

NASB.1: Now Abraham took another wife, whose name was Keturah.
NASB.2: She bore to him Zimran and Jokshan and Medan and Midian and Ishbak and Shuah.
NASB.3: Jokshan became the father of Sheba and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were Asshurim and Letushim and Leummim.
NASB.4: The sons of Midian [were] Ephah and Epher and Hanoch and Abida and Eldaah. All these [were] the sons of Keturah.
NASB.5: Now Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac;
NASB.6: but to the sons of his concubines, Abraham gave gifts while he was still living, and sent them away from his son Isaac eastward, to the land of the east.
NASB.7: These are all the years of Abraham's life that he lived, one hundred and seventy-five years.
NASB.8: Abraham breathed his last and died in a ripe old age, an old man and satisfied [with life]; and he was gathered to his people.
NASB.9: Then his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, facing Mamre,
NASB.10: the field which Abraham purchased from the sons of Heth; there Abraham was buried with Sarah his wife.
NASB.11: It came about after the death of Abraham, that God blessed his son Isaac; and Isaac lived by Beer-lahai-roi.
NASB.12: Now these are [the records of] the generations of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's maid, bore to Abraham;
NASB.13: and these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, in the order of their birth: Nebaioth, the firstborn of Ishmael, and Kedar and Adbeel and Mibsam
NASB.14: and Mishma and Dumah and Massa,
NASB.15: Hadad and Tema, Jetur, Naphish and Kedemah.
NASB.16: These are the sons of Ishmael and these are their names, by their villages, and by their camps; twelve princes according to their tribes.
NASB.17: These are the years of the life of Ishmael, one hundred and thirty-seven years; and he breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people.
NASB.18: They settled from Havilah to Shur which is east of Egypt as one goes toward Assyria; he settled in defiance of all his relatives.
NASB.19: Now these are [the records of] the generations of Isaac, Abraham's son: Abraham became the father of Isaac;
NASB.20: and Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean of Paddan-aram, the sister of Laban the Aramean, to be his wife.

NASB.23: The LORD said to her, 'Two nations are in your womb; And two peoples will be separated from your body; And one people shall be stronger than the other; And the older shall serve the younger.'
NASB.24: When her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb.
NASB.25: Now the first came forth red, all over like a hairy garment; and they named him Esau.
NASB.26: Afterward his brother came forth with his hand holding on to Esau's heel, so his name was called Jacob; and Isaac was sixty years old when she gave birth to them.
NASB.27: When the boys grew up, Esau became a skillful hunter, a man of the field, but Jacob was a peaceful man, living in tents.
NASB.28: Now Isaac loved Esau, because he had a taste for game, but Rebekah loved Jacob.
NASB.29: When Jacob had cooked stew, Esau came in from the field and he was famished;

NASB.33: And Jacob said, 'First swear to me'; so he swore to him, and sold his birthright to Jacob.

ESV.1: Abraham took another wife, whose name was Keturah.
ESV.2: She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
ESV.3: Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan. The sons of Dedan were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
ESV.4: The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah.
ESV.5: Abraham gave all he had to Isaac.
ESV.6: But to the sons of his concubines Abraham gave gifts, and while he was still living he sent them away from his son Isaac, eastward to the east country.
ESV.7: These are the days of the years of Abraham's life, 175 years.
ESV.8: Abraham breathed his last and died in a good old age, an old man and full of years, and was gathered to his people.
ESV.9: Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, east of Mamre,
ESV.10: the field that Abraham purchased from the Hittites. There Abraham was buried, with Sarah his wife.
ESV.11: After the death of Abraham, God blessed Isaac his son. And Isaac settled at Beer-lahai-roi.
ESV.12: These are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's servant, bore to Abraham.
ESV.13: These are the names of the sons of Ishmael, named in the order of their birth: Nebaioth, the firstborn of Ishmael; and Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
ESV.15: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
ESV.16: These are the sons of Ishmael and these are their names, by their villages and by their encampments, twelve princes according to their tribes.
ESV.17: (These are the years of the life of Ishmael: 137 years. He breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people.)
ESV.18: They settled from Havilah to Shur, which is opposite Egypt in the direction of Assyria. He settled  over against all his kinsmen.
ESV.19: These are the generations of Isaac, Abraham's son: Abraham fathered Isaac,
ESV.20: and Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean of Paddan-aram, the sister of Laban the Aramean, to be his wife.
ESV.21: And Isaac prayed to the LORD for his wife, because she was barren. And the LORD granted his prayer, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
ESV.22: The children struggled together within her, and she said, “If it is thus, why is this happening to me?”  So she went to inquire of the LORD.
ESV.23: And the LORD said to her, “Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from within you  shall be divided; the one shall be stronger than the other, the older shall serve the younger.”
ESV.24: When her days to give birth were completed, behold, there were twins in her womb.
ESV.25: The first came out red, all his body like a hairy cloak, so they called his name Esau.
ESV.26: Afterward his brother came out with his hand holding Esau's heel, so his name was called Jacob.  Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them.
ESV.27: When the boys grew up, Esau was a skillful hunter, a man of the field, while Jacob was a quiet man, dwelling in tents.
ESV.28: Isaac loved Esau because he ate of his game, but Rebekah loved Jacob.
ESV.29: Once when Jacob was cooking stew, Esau came in from the field, and he was exhausted.
ESV.30: And Esau said to Jacob, “Let me eat some of that red stew, for I am exhausted!” (Therefore his name was called Edom. )
ESV.31: Jacob said, “Sell me your birthright now.”
ESV.32: Esau said, “I am about to die; of what use is a birthright to me?”
ESV.33: Jacob said, “Swear to me now.” So he swore to him and sold his birthright to Jacob.
ESV.34: Then Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew, and he ate and drank and rose and went his way. Thus Esau despised his birthright.

NLT.1: Abraham married another wife, whose name was Keturah.
NLT.2: She gave birth to Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
NLT.3: Jokshan was the father of Sheba and Dedan. Dedan’s descendants were the Asshurites, Letushites, and Leummites.
NLT.4: Midian’s sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. These were all descendants of Abraham through Keturah.
NLT.5: Abraham gave everything he owned to his son Isaac.
NLT.6: But before he died, he gave gifts to the sons of his concubines and sent them off to a land in the east, away from Isaac.
NLT.8: and he died at a ripe old age, having lived a long and satisfying life. He breathed his last and joined his ancestors in death.
NLT.9: His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, near Mamre, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite.
NLT.10: This was the field Abraham had purchased from the Hittites and where he had buried his wife Sarah.
NLT.11: After Abraham’s death, God blessed his son Isaac, who settled near Beer-lahai-roi in the Negev.
NLT.12: This is the account of the family of Ishmael, the son of Abraham through Hagar, Sarah’s Egyptian servant.
NLT.13: Here is a list, by their names and clans, of Ishmael’s descendants: The oldest was Nebaioth, followed by Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
NLT.15: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
NLT.16: These twelve sons of Ishmael became the founders of twelve tribes named after them, listed according to the places they settled and camped.
NLT.17: Ishmael lived for 137 years. Then he breathed his last and joined his ancestors in death.
NLT.18: Ishmael’s descendants occupied the region from Havilah to Shur, which is east of Egypt in the direction of Asshur. There they lived in open hostility toward all their relatives.
NLT.19: This is the account of the family of Isaac, the son of Abraham.
NLT.20: When Isaac was forty years old, he married Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan-aram and the sister of Laban the Aramean.
NLT.21: Isaac pleaded with the LORD on behalf of his wife, because she was unable to have children. The LORD answered Isaac’s prayer, and Rebekah became pregnant with twins.
NLT.22: But the two children struggled with each other in her womb. So she went to ask the LORD about it. “Why is this happening to me?” she asked.
NLT.23: And the LORD told her, “The sons in your womb will become two nations. From the very beginning, the two nations will be rivals. One nation will be stronger than the other; and your older son will serve your younger son.”
NLT.24: And when the time came to give birth, Rebekah discovered that she did indeed have twins!
NLT.25: The first one was very red at birth and covered with thick hair like a fur coat. So they named him Esau.
NLT.26: Then the other twin was born with his hand grasping Esau’s heel. So they named him Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when the twins were born.
NLT.27: As the boys grew up, Esau became a skillful hunter. He was an outdoorsman, but Jacob had a quiet temperament, preferring to stay at home.
NLT.28: Isaac loved Esau because he enjoyed eating the wild game Esau brought home, but Rebekah loved Jacob.
NLT.29: One day when Jacob was cooking some stew, Esau arrived home from the wilderness exhausted and hungry.

AMP.1: Abraham took another wife, whose name was Keturah.
AMP.2: She gave birth to Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
AMP.3: Jokshan was the father of Sheba and Dedan. The sons of Dedan were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
AMP.4: The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the sons of Keturah.
AMP.5: Now Abraham gave everything that he had to Isaac;
AMP.6: but to the sons of his concubines [Hagar and Keturah], Abraham gave gifts while he was still living and he sent them to the east country, away from Isaac his son [of promise].
AMP.7: The days of Abraham's life were a hundred and seventy-five years.
AMP.8: Then Abraham breathed his last and he died at a good old age, an old man who was satisfied [with life]; and he was gathered to his people [who had preceded him in death].
AMP.9: So his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, which is east of Mamre,
AMP.10: the field which Abraham purchased from the sons of Heth; there Abraham was buried with Sarah his wife.
AMP.11: Now after the death of Abraham, God blessed his son Isaac; and Isaac lived at Beer-lahai-roi.
AMP.12: Now these are the records of the descendants of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's maid, bore to Abraham;
AMP.13: and these are the names of the [twelve] sons of Ishmael, named in the order of their births: Nebaioth, the firstborn of Ishmael, and Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
AMP.15: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
AMP.16: These are the sons of Ishmael and these are their names, by their settlements, and by their encampments (sheepfolds); twelve princes (sheiks) according to their tribes.
AMP.17: Ishmael lived a hundred and thirty-seven years; then he breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people [who had preceded him in death].
AMP.18: Ishmael's sons (descendants) settled from Havilah to Shur which is east of Egypt as one goes toward Assyria; he settled opposite (east) of all his relatives.
AMP.19: Now these are the records of the descendants of Isaac, Abraham's son: Abraham was the father of Isaac.
AMP.20: Isaac was forty years old when he married Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean (Syrian) of Paddan-aram, the sister of Laban the Aramean.
AMP.21: Isaac prayed to the LORD for his wife, because she was unable to conceive children; and the LORD granted his prayer and Rebekah his wife conceived [twins].
AMP.22: But the children struggled together within her [kicking and shoving one another]; and she said, "If it is so [that the LORD has heard our prayer], why then am I this way?" So she went to inquire of the LORD [praying for an answer].
AMP.23:
The LORD said to her,
"[The founders of] two nations are in your womb;
And the separation of two nations has begun in your body;

AMP.24: When her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb.
AMP.25: The first came out reddish all over like a hairy garment; and they named him Esau (hairy).
AMP.26: Afterward his brother came out, and his hand grasped Esau's heel, so he was named Jacob ( one who grabs by the heel, supplanter). Isaac was sixty years old when Rebekah gave birth to them.
AMP.27: When the boys grew up, Esau was an able and skilled hunter, a man of the outdoors, but Jacob was a quiet and peaceful man, living in tents.
AMP.28: Now Isaac loved [and favored] Esau, because he enjoyed eating his game, but Rebekah loved [and favored] Jacob.
AMP.29: Jacob had cooked [reddish-brown lentil] stew [one day], when Esau came from the field and was famished;
AMP.30: and Esau said to Jacob, "Please, let me have a quick swallow of that red stuff there, because I am exhausted and famished." For that reason Esau was [also] called Edom (Red).
AMP.31: Jacob answered, "First sell me your birthright (the rights of a firstborn)."
AMP.32: Esau said, "Look, I am about to die [if I do not eat soon]; so of what use is this birthright to me?"
AMP.33: Jacob said, "Swear [an oath] to me today [that you are selling it to me for this food]"; so he swore [an oath] to him, and sold him his birthright.
AMP.34: Then Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew; and he ate and drank, and got up and went on his way. In this way Esau scorned his birthright.

NET.17: Ishmael lived a total of 137 years. He breathed his last and died; then he joined his ancestors.
NET.18: His descendants settled from Havilah to Shur, which runs next to Egypt all the way to Asshur. They settled away from all their relatives.
NET.19: This is the account of Isaac, the son of Abraham. Abraham became the father of Isaac.
NET.20: When Isaac was forty years old, he married Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan Aram and sister of Laban the Aramean.
NET.21: Isaac prayed to the LORD on behalf of his wife because she was childless. The LORD answered his prayer, and his wife Rebekah became pregnant.
NET.22: But the children struggled inside her, and she said, “If it is going to be like this, I’m not so sure I want to be pregnant!” So she asked the LORD,
NET.23: and the LORD said to her, “Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will be separated from within you. One people will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger.”
NET.24: When the time came for Rebekah to give birth, there were twins in her womb.
NET.25: The first came out reddish all over, like a hairy garment, so they named him Esau.
NET.26: When his brother came out with his hand clutching Esau’s heel, they named him Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when they were born.
NET.27: When the boys grew up, Esau became a skilled hunter, a man of the open fields, but Jacob was an even-tempered man, living in tents.
NET.28: Isaac loved Esau because he had a taste for fresh game, but Rebekah loved Jacob.
NET.29: Now Jacob cooked some stew, and when Esau came in from the open fields, he was famished.
NET.30: So Esau said to Jacob, “Feed me some of the red stuff — yes, this red stuff — because I’m starving!” (That is why he was also called Edom.)
NET.31: But Jacob replied, “First sell me your birthright.”
NET.32: “Look,” said Esau, “I’m about to die! What use is the birthright to me?”
NET.33: But Jacob said, “Swear an oath to me now.” So Esau swore an oath to him and sold his birthright to Jacob.
NET.34: Then Jacob gave Esau some bread and lentil stew; Esau ate and drank, then got up and went out. So Esau despised his birthright.
